title: Conjugate transformations of adjoint functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories and $L_1\dashv R_1$, $L_2\dashv R_2$ two adjunctions with $L_i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $R_i:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, units $\eta_i$ and counits $\varepsilon_i$. For a natural transformation $\tau:L_2\to L_1$ its *conjugate* is the natural transformation $\tau^c:R_1\to R_2$ with components
$$
 R_1d\xrightarrow{\eta_{2,R_1d}}R_2L_2R_1d\xrightarrow{R_2\tau_{R_1d}}R_2L_1R_1d\xrightarrow{R_2\varepsilon_{1,d}}R_2d ,
$$
i.e. the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $\tau$ for $G=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$, $H=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$. The assignment $\tau\mapsto\tau^c$ is a bijection; it is compatible with composition, $(\tau\circ\tau')^c=\tau'^c\circ\tau^c$ for $\tau':L_3\to L_2$ and a third adjunction $L_3\dashv R_3$, and sends $\mathrm{id}_{L}$ to $\mathrm{id}_R$ for one adjunction $L\dashv R$. Consequently $\tau$ is an isomorphism if and only if $\tau^c$ is, and for an isomorphism $\tau$ one has $(\tau^{-1})^c=(\tau^c)^{-1}$; this gives a bijection between isomorphisms $L_2\cong L_1$ and isomorphisms $R_1\cong R_2$.
